summary: Light at the end of Victoria's Ogden Point breakwater: built with the federal harbour works around 1914-1917, first shown in 1917 from an unwatched beacon, and open for walking today.

structures.note: Square tapered concrete tower, white with a broad red band at the base (Rowlett; Coast Guard 'White tower with red band at bottom'). LighthouseFriends describes the 1917 tower as square, white and pyramidal, with an occulting white light 40 ft above high water.

access.note: Walk out the breakwater (nearly 800 m, handrails, a flat path). The tower is closed to visitors; grounds open.

events.note: Government decides to improve Victoria's shipping facilities after a preliminary study by Louis Coste (CSCE).
Breakwater and docks construction; a 1914-15 appropriation of $1,100,000 provided the first money (LighthouseFriends). CSCE dates construction 1914-1917.
Breakwater and docks completed in 1917 (Victoria Heritage Foundation; CSCE). LighthouseFriends and Tourism Victoria give 1916.
Unwatched acetylene beacon erected under a contract to Parfitt Brothers at $1,655 (fiscal 1916-17 report); LighthouseFriends says a square white pyramidal concrete tower followed.
Electrically operated fog alarm installed at Ogden Point (report for fiscal 1918-19; LighthouseFriends says 1919).
A cable from shore supplies electricity to the breakwater (LighthouseFriends).
Named a National Historic Civil Engineering Site; plaque unveiled on the walkway on 2 May 2001.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three versions: the current Coast Guard list gives quick-flashing red (Q R 1s); Wikidata gives Fl R 1s; LighthouseFriends describes the 1917 light as an occulting white light. The Coast Guard list is taken as current. The sources read do not date the change from white to red.

The breakwater's completion year is 1916 in LighthouseFriends and Tourism Victoria, and 1917 in the Victoria Heritage Foundation and the Canadian Society for Civil Engineering. The story gives both. The light followed in 1917 on any reading.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. LighthouseFriends (5) is a copyrighted community site, used for facts only and paraphrased. The Victoria Heritage Foundation (3) and the Canadian Society for Civil Engineering (4) are heritage and engineering records; they give the best detail on the works. Tourism Victoria (7) is a promotional page, used only for the path's length and character. Rowlett (6) is a directory.

Disagreements left open: (a) completion year, 1916 or 1917 (see resolved_conflicts); (b) granite source: LighthouseFriends says Hardy Island only; the Canadian Society for Civil Engineering names Haddington, Nelson and Hardy islands. The story gives both. (c) Characteristic: the 1917 light was an occulting white light (LighthouseFriends), now a quick-flashing red light (Coast Guard list, Rowlett). The change is not dated in any source read. (d) The Public Works appropriation of 1914-15 ($1.1 million) comes from LighthouseFriends only; I did not find the Public Works report that would confirm it. (e) The $1,655 Parfitt contract: the 1916-17 report names it for 'Erection of an unwatched acetylene beacon'; LighthouseFriends says Parfitt Brothers erected the tower at that price. The story states both and does not settle which.

Death tolls. The Clallam (1904, 55) and Sechelt (1911, 58) figures come from the Victoria Heritage Foundation alone, and are attributed to it in the story. Neither loss is recorded here as a station event.

Unwatched from the start. The 1916-17 Department report lists an unwatched acetylene beacon, so the roster is empty and no keepers are recorded. No wreck or rescue tied to the light turned up in the sources read, so no wrecks entry is given.

Fiscal years. The Marine report labelled 1920 (scan 98) covers fiscal 1918-19, the year to 31 March 1919. The fog-alarm year is therefore 1918-19 in the Department's report and 1919 in LighthouseFriends.

Not reached: Nauticapedia's article on the breakwater returned 403, and I did not read it. The Victoria City Archives item and the focusonvictoria.ca history were found by search but not read.

No photos added. The record's Commons image was not checked for licence.
